about: Ten fixed prompts, each with the answer this skill is expected to give, and the facts that answer needs. tools/lumin/src/skills.test.ts checks that every fact appears in the skill's own text (SKILL.md and references/), so the skill cannot drift away from its answers.

cases.prompt: The hero title should rise in when the page loads and settle. What do you set?
cases.answer: A time-driven track on hero-title.transform.position.y plus opacity, triggered by load: 24 px to 0 over 0.8 s with the enter token, then settle. Supporting copy 120 ms later over 0.6 s, the action last. Rest pose is opacity 1, y 0.

cases.prompt: A row of cards should reveal as the visitor scrolls past, and not replay when they scroll back.
cases.answer: An in-view trigger, once, at a third of the block visible: 16 px rise and opacity 0 to 1 over 0.5 s with enter, 60 ms stagger between cards, no replay.

cases.prompt: How does the scene behave under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce?
cases.answer: Every stage shows the rest pose and draws no animation frames; pointer and hover tracks do not run; a scrubbed scene snaps to the nearest chapter and holds it; content stays visible.

cases.prompt: The camera should move across chapters as the page scrolls, backwards too.
cases.answer: A scroll-driven track scrubbed by progress between composed camera keyframes, linear easing, with the damping in the conductor: measured anchors, a smooth copy of progress, a step clamped to 1/30 s, paused while hidden.

cases.prompt: Which durations and easings do we use?
cases.answer: The token package's fast 120 ms, base 200 ms and slow 320 ms, extended by class: 180 to 260 ms for UI state, 220 to 320 ms for a popover, 400 to 800 ms for a section, 800 to 1600 ms for a hero, and the easings enter, exit, settle, standard and linear.

cases.prompt: A card should tilt a little as the pointer moves over it.
cases.answer: A pointer-driven track on the card's rotation, running only while hovered or focused, with a rest pose of 0, and never moving the scroll story.

cases.prompt: A stage is scrolled out of view. What should it cost?
cases.answer: Zero frames: an intersection observer stops it, the hidden document stops it too, and the frame counter stays flat until it returns.

cases.prompt: An agent wrote a track with target hero-title.position.y. What happens?
cases.answer: It is refused with the path: a property path names a node and a property the node has, and the transform names its channels, so hero-title.transform.position.y is the path.

cases.prompt: A button should lift on hover and come back down when the pointer leaves.
cases.answer: A hover-triggered track: 2 to 6 px lift over about 120 to 200 ms with the standard token, returning to the rest pose on leave or blur, with no bounce.

cases.prompt: Can I write a track into a scene document today?
cases.answer: Not yet: tracks are the v2 document, which lands in G4; the runtime and its triggers in G5; emission and the playground in G6. A v1 document has no tracks and must not pretend to.
